Name: Business checking
Notes: Commission deposits land here; business costs paid from here

Name: Tax savings
Notes: Money set aside for estimated tax. Keeps it from looking like spending money

Name: Business credit card
Notes: One card for business costs only

Name: Owner draws
Notes: Money moved to your personal account. Not an expense

Name: Estimated tax payments
Notes: Federal estimates paid from the business account. Not an expense

Name: Gross commission income
Notes: Your side of each closing, before the brokerage split and fees

Name: Referral fees received
Notes: From agents you send clients to

Name: Brokerage split
Notes: The brokerage's share of your side of the commission

Name: Transaction fees
Notes: Per-closing fees the brokerage takes from the check

Name: Referral fees paid
Notes: Get a Form W-9 before paying. 1099-NEC at $2000 or more for payments from 2026

Name: Team member commissions
Notes: Team leads only: each member's share when the whole commission is paid to the lead

Name: Desk fees
Notes: Monthly brokerage desk or office fee

Name: E&O insurance
Notes: Including per-transaction E&O fees taken from a commission check

Name: Marketing
Notes: Listing photos, signs, print, listing ads

Name: Lead generation
Notes: Paid lead services and online ads for buyers and sellers

Name: Vehicle
Notes: Fuel and car costs. Keep a mileage log; your tax preparer decides how the car is deducted

Name: Client gifts
Notes: Book the full cost with the person's name. Deduction limited to $25 per person per year (IRS Publication 463)
